forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Worcester Council behind on five audit recommendations on spending controls
news_drafts.lead: Worcester Council's Audit and Governance Committee was told the council has 19 outstanding internal audit recommendations, of which 5 are overdue. The overdue findings cover transparency code publication, reporting of purchasing card spending, and contract management monitoring. The council has implemented 74 per cent of recommendations overall, just below its 75 per cent target. The recommendations follow audits of the council's financial controls and procurement processes.

findings.headline: Non-treasury loans are recorded below their original amounts, with the Kiln CIC loan at £2,250 against £20,000 originally lent.
findings.detail: The council holds £14,257,882 of non-treasury investments, including directly owned property of £11,461,000. Four loans are shown with current balances below their original amounts: Worcestershire F.A. (£651,139 from £750,000), Lower Wick Swimming Pool (£71,934 from £97,800), Kiln CIC (£2,250 from £20,000) and the Worcester International Hockey JV (£2,071,559 from £2.1m). The paper does not explain the reductions.
findings.matters: Reductions in the carrying value of loans to community and sports bodies show where the council's non-treasury lending has moved from its original terms, which is relevant to how other councils value similar exposures.
findings.figures: £14,257,882 total non-treasury investments; £11,461,000 directly owned property; Kiln CIC £2,250 (originally £20,000); Lower Wick £71,934 (originally £97,800); Worcestershire F.A. £651,139 (originally £750,000); Hockey JV £2,071,559 (originally £2.1m)

findings.headline: The CCLA Property Fund holding, purchased at £3.0m, was valued at approximately £2.6m at 30 September 2026, an unrealised loss of around £0.4m.
findings.detail: The paper says the IFRS 9 statutory override has been extended to 31 March 2029, so the loss does not currently affect the General Fund. If the override is not extended beyond that date, the council may need to recognise a one-off charge of about £400,000 in 2029/30. No provision has been made.
findings.matters: An unprovided potential charge tied to a statutory override expiry is a contingent liability a finance director or lender would want to track against the council's reserves.
findings.figures: £3.0m investment; approximately £2.6m market value at 30.09.26; around £0.4m unrealised loss; approximately £400,000 potential charge in 2029/30; override extended to 31 March 2029
findings.quote: At 30 September 2026, the market value of this investment was approximately £2.6m, representing an unrealised capital loss of around £0.4m.

findings.headline: The General Fund Capital Financing Requirement is forecast to rise from £31.4m to £37.7m by 31 March 2027, alongside a 2026/27 capital programme of £21.086m.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the increase to capital programme expenditure funded through prudential borrowing. Largest 2026/27 forecast items include Future High Streets/Levelling Up at £8.641m and the Crematorium Refurbishment at £3.298m.
findings.matters: A growing CFR means the council's underlying need to borrow is rising, which will require more external funding in the coming years.
findings.figures: CFR £31.4m (31.03.26) to £37.7m (31.03.27 forecast); 2026/27 capital expenditure forecast £21.086m; Future High Streets/Levelling Up £8.641m; Crematorium Refurbishment £3.298m
findings.quote: The forecast position indicates that the General Fund CFR will increase from £31.4m at 31 March 2026 to £37.7m by 31 March 2027.

findings.headline: Annual borrowing costs are forecast at £598,290 for 2026/27, up from £441,124 in 2025/26.
findings.detail: The paper gives the 2026/27 forecast for annual borrowing costs and states that the average interest rate on the council's borrowing portfolio is currently 3.43%. Financing costs are shown at 10.61% of net revenue stream for 2026/27 and rising to 14.01% in the 2027/28 budget.
findings.matters: A rise in financing costs as a share of the revenue stream shows how much of the budget the council is committing to debt service as its borrowing grows.
findings.figures: £598,290 forecast 2026/27 borrowing costs; £441,124 in 2025/26; average interest rate 3.43%; financing costs 10.61% (2026/27 forecast), 14.01% (2027/28 budget)
findings.quote: Annual borrowing costs are forecast to be £598,290, compared with £441,124 in 2025/26.

findings.headline: The £5.0m LOBO loan, taken for 50 years from 3 December 2004, has its next option date on 3 December 2026.
findings.detail: The paper treats LOBO option dates as potential repayment dates and shows the £5.0m balance unchanged at 30 September 2026. The paper does not report any lender exercise of the option, and the 3 December 2026 date falls after the report was written. The lender is not named.
findings.matters: A lender option on a £5.0m loan within weeks is a potential repayment and replacement event for the council, which affects its cash needs and replacement funding costs.
findings.figures: £5.0m LOBO balance; 50-year term from 3 December 2004; next option date 3 December 2026
findings.quote: LOBO option dates are treated as potential repayment dates, the next being 3rd December

daily_post.headline: Rent and hosting costs rise in 2027/28, and the Wyre Forest contract ties the rent and ICT element to RPI, so the figure may change in April 2027.
daily_post.lead: Hosting and rent costs linked to an index are not fixed at budget setting, so partner contributions can move after the budget is agreed.
